name: Training Networks
strandNote: Not needed for the quant path. Machine learning research roles, and reading deep learning papers.
description: Make a network train fast and generalise, and run experiments whose conclusions survive a new seed.

requires.why: Every optimiser here updates the parameters of the NumPy array autograd built in that level.
Builds on its minibatches and learning-rate sweep instead of reteaching them.
Momentum and Adam are judged against the step-size limit from curvature in l14.
Initialisation keeps activations steady using the variance of a sum of independent terms.
Batch normalisation extends standardising features before fitting, from l9.
Weight decay is the ridge penalty of l7, applied to a network's weights.
Early stopping and dropout rates are chosen on a validation set, as in l1 and l3.
The interpolating fit in double descent is the pseudoinverse's minimum-norm solution; a quick check helps.
Two configurations are compared across seeds with the paired test from l8.
Trying many configurations is multiple testing, as in l9 and l12.

lessonNames.l6-initialisation: Starting weights that keep the signal
lessonNames.l15-training-log: A training log you can audit

lessonObjectives.l1-noisy-steps: Explain how the batch size sets the noise in a gradient step, and pick a learning rate from a loss curve.
lessonObjectives.l2-momentum: Write momentum and show how it speeds descent along a long, narrow valley.
lessonObjectives.l3-adam: Write Adam with its bias correction, and say what each moment estimate does.
lessonObjectives.l4-schedules: Build warm-up and cosine decay schedules, and judge them by final loss.
lessonObjectives.l5-saturation: Explain why saturating activations and deep products of small slopes make gradients vanish.
lessonObjectives.l6-initialisation: Derive the weight scale that keeps activation variance steady through a layer.
lessonObjectives.l7-batch-norm: Write batch normalisation for training and for inference, and see what it does to a deep net.
lessonObjectives.l8-layer-norm: Write layer normalisation with its backward pass, and say when it is preferred to batch normalisation.
lessonObjectives.l9-weight-decay: Show that weight decay is the ridge penalty, and choose its strength on validation loss.
lessonObjectives.l10-early-stopping: Stop training at the best validation loss, and read early stopping as a penalty on steps.
lessonObjectives.l11-dropout: Write inverted dropout and explain why the network is scaled at training time.
lessonObjectives.l12-double-descent: Explain the second fall in test error once parameters outnumber data points.
lessonObjectives.l13-one-seed-one-draw: Measure the spread of a result across seeds before believing one run.
lessonObjectives.l14-ablations: Design an ablation that removes one change at a time, and read which change mattered.
lessonObjectives.l15-training-log: Build a training log that records everything a rerun needs, and audit one.
lessonObjectives.l16-paired-seeds: Compare two training set-ups across seeds with a paired test and a confidence interval.
